technique: Indirect prompt injection via retrieved content
objective: Place benign adversarial instructions in a controlled test document and determine whether retrieved text changes agent behavior beyond its data role.
safe_test_method: Use a synthetic corpus and harmless canary action; compare baseline vs injected retrieval.
evidence: Retrieved source, prompt/context trace, tool-call delta, policy outcome.
mitigation: Treat retrieved content as untrusted data; isolate instructions from data; provenance and output checks.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Assess whether user input or retrieved content can cause disclosure of confidential instruction text or internal configuration.
safe_test_method: Use synthetic system instructions containing a unique canary phrase; test disclosure boundaries.
evidence: Exact canary exposure, request trace, model/version, repeatability.
mitigation: Keep secrets out of prompts; separate policy from prompt; restrict diagnostic output.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Determine whether an agent can invoke tools or arguments beyond the user's intended task and role.
safe_test_method: Use mock tools with harmless read/write fixtures; compare role-specific tool availability.
evidence: Tool catalog, role, requested args, authorization decision, side effect.
mitigation: Least privilege, per-tool authorization, schema validation, human approval for sensitive actions.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Test whether malformed, ambiguous or extra arguments bypass tool validation or alter meaning.
safe_test_method: Fuzz JSON schemas in a local harness; assert rejection of unknown or invalid fields.
evidence: Request/response pair, validation result, downstream effect.
mitigation: Strict schemas, reject unknown fields, canonicalization, typed wrappers.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Check whether file tools enforce approved roots and normalize paths consistently.
safe_test_method: Use a temporary sandbox directory with decoy files; test traversal strings without accessing host files.
evidence: Resolved path, policy decision, sandbox logs.
mitigation: Canonical path checks, directory handles, sandboxed filesystem, deny-by-default.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Assess whether a URL tool can reach prohibited network destinations or cloud metadata endpoints.
safe_test_method: Use a local mock network with controlled internal canary endpoints; no production metadata access.
evidence: Destination, DNS resolution, redirect chain, egress log.
mitigation: Egress proxy, destination allowlist, DNS/IP validation, redirect revalidation.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Verify tenant filters are enforced at retrieval and reranking, not merely in the UI.
safe_test_method: Seed synthetic tenant A/B records with unique canaries and test all retrieval paths.
evidence: Tenant identity, query, returned IDs, ACL metadata.
mitigation: Server-side ACL enforcement, tenant-scoped indexes, negative regression tests.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Test whether unauthorized or low-trust content can enter the corpus and influence answers.
safe_test_method: Ingest tagged synthetic documents through test pipeline; track source lineage and approval.
evidence: Document hash, uploader, parser, chunk IDs, retrieval frequency.
mitigation: Signed/provenanced ingestion, approval gates, source trust labels, quarantine.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Assess whether embeddings or similarity APIs expose sensitive attributes or reveal membership.
safe_test_method: Use synthetic datasets and canary records; measure inference success without real personal data.
evidence: Dataset, model, query, confidence, leakage rate.
mitigation: Minimize stored metadata, access controls, privacy review, retention and query controls.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Check whether one session can influence another or persist untrusted instructions in shared memory.
safe_test_method: Use isolated test accounts and synthetic memory markers; test persistence and deletion.
evidence: Session IDs, memory writes/reads, retention behavior.
mitigation: Namespace memory by principal/tenant; provenance, TTL, write authorization, deletion semantics.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Assess integrity and authorization around serialized state, checkpoints and resumed workflows.
safe_test_method: Use local test checkpoint store and signed synthetic state; test stale/replayed versions.
evidence: Checkpoint hash, version, principal, resume decision.
mitigation: Integrity protection, access control, versioning, replay protection, secret minimization.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Determine whether an untrusted endpoint can claim another agent identity or capability set.
safe_test_method: Use two mock agents and a local discovery registry; validate identity binding.
evidence: Agent Card, endpoint identity, signature/trust decision.
mitigation: Authenticated discovery, signed metadata, trust registry, audience binding.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Check whether delegated tasks inherit more authority than the originating principal granted.
safe_test_method: Use mock agents with read-only and admin-like dummy tools; test capability attenuation.
evidence: Delegation token claims, parent/child scope, authorization result.
mitigation: Capability attenuation, audience/scope binding, expiry, explicit delegation policy.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Assess whether tool metadata can manipulate agent selection or induce unsafe parameter use.
safe_test_method: Use a local MCP server with clearly labelled synthetic tool descriptions and harmless tools.
evidence: Tool metadata, model selection, selected args, user confirmation.
mitigation: Treat metadata as untrusted; server identity verification; curated tool registry.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Review transport security, authentication, session binding, origin checks and authorization on each call.
safe_test_method: Use local test server and protocol test harness; test unauthenticated and wrong-principal calls.
evidence: Transport trace, identity, session, authorization outcome.
mitigation: TLS, strong auth, per-call authorization, session binding, origin controls.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Identify unsafe serialization formats and loading paths in model or ML pipelines.
safe_test_method: Static review and isolated toy artifact tests; never load untrusted artifacts on a workstation.
evidence: Artifact format, loader path, dependency versions, sandbox result.
mitigation: Prefer safe formats, signed artifacts, isolated loaders, pinned dependencies.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Validate model weights, LoRA adapters, tokenizer files and configuration integrity.
safe_test_method: Compare hashes/signatures against an approved manifest in a test registry.
evidence: Artifact hash, signer, registry history, mismatch evidence.
mitigation: Signed manifests, immutable registries, reproducible builds, provenance checks.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Assess dataset ingestion, labeling, provenance and anomaly review for malicious or low-quality records.
safe_test_method: Use synthetic labelled examples and controlled data-quality anomalies.
evidence: Dataset lineage, labels, approval history, detection outcome.
mitigation: Dataset versioning, provenance, anomaly checks, review and rollback.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Map whether a compromised workload identity could reach unrelated resources or privileged APIs.
safe_test_method: Use cloud test account and non-production resources; inspect policy and simulate denied/allowed calls.
evidence: Principal, policy, resource, API result, path.
mitigation: Workload identity scoping, short-lived credentials, resource conditions, least privilege.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Check whether pod service accounts and RBAC grant excessive cluster or namespace permissions.
safe_test_method: Use a disposable cluster and synthetic service accounts; use read-only discovery first.
evidence: Pod, service account, RoleBinding, effective permissions.
mitigation: Dedicated service accounts, minimal RBAC, automount controls, network policies.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Assess untrusted pull-request triggers, token permissions, artifact promotion and secret exposure.
safe_test_method: Review workflow configuration and test in fork/sandbox pipelines with dummy secrets.
evidence: Trigger source, token scope, artifact provenance, log exposure.
mitigation: Least-privilege tokens, protected environments, OIDC, provenance and approval gates.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Check object-level authorization across users and tenants for read/update/delete operations.
safe_test_method: Use two synthetic users and seeded objects in a staging environment.
evidence: Principal A/B, object owner, operation, response and audit log.
mitigation: Centralized object authorization, tenant binding, negative tests.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Compare field-, resolver- and object-level authorization across query and mutation paths.
safe_test_method: Use a staging schema and synthetic roles/data; introspection only where authorized.
evidence: Schema path, role, resolver response, access decision.
mitigation: Resolver-level authorization, depth/complexity limits, schema governance.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Review issuer, audience, expiry, algorithm, key rotation and claim-to-role mapping.
safe_test_method: Use test keys and synthetic tokens; no production token forgery or replay.
evidence: Token claims (redacted), validation configuration, result.
mitigation: Strict algorithm/key policy, issuer/audience checks, short expiry, rotation.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Test whether workflows enforce required state transitions and approvals server-side.
safe_test_method: Create synthetic transactions and test invalid transitions in staging.
evidence: State machine, actor, requested transition, server result.
mitigation: Server-side invariants, idempotency, approval enforcement, audit trail.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Find secrets, personal data or tenant content in application logs, traces, prompts and model telemetry.
safe_test_method: Use synthetic markers; inspect test observability pipelines.
evidence: Marker, sink, retention, access policy.
mitigation: Redaction before logging, minimization, access controls, retention limits.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Assess quotas, concurrency, context size, tool loops and retry behavior without stressing production.
safe_test_method: Use low-rate bounded tests in staging with hard stop thresholds.
evidence: Request rate, latency, queue depth, cost, stop event.
mitigation: Per-principal quotas, circuit breakers, budgets, loop limits, graceful degradation.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Check whether cached responses or retrieval results cross user/tenant boundaries or persist stale permissions.
safe_test_method: Use synthetic users and cache keys in staging; test invalidation after ACL changes.
evidence: Cache key, principal, content marker, invalidation trace.
mitigation: Principal-aware cache keys, ACL-aware invalidation, short TTL, no shared sensitive cache.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Review parser isolation, MIME/content validation, archive handling and document conversion paths.
safe_test_method: Use harmless malformed test files in isolated ingestion pipeline.
evidence: File hash/type, parser, sandbox logs, rejection/acceptance.
mitigation: Sandbox parsers, resource limits, content validation, malware scanning.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.

objective: Determine whether key test behaviors produce useful telemetry and actionable alerts.
safe_test_method: Replay safe synthetic events mapped to agreed detections.
evidence: Event IDs, alert, time-to-detect, response owner.
mitigation: Telemetry normalization, detection tuning, runbooks, measurable coverage.
engagement_control: Run only against explicitly approved assets and identities; use synthetic data and bounded proofs where possible.
